ledger.note: 3200 BCE: the Uruk colonies are deserted. "after 3300/3200 BC this dynamic ceased and the Near East became culturally more fragmented"; "the colonial sites have been deserted (probably before the changes at Uruk)"; Habuba Kabira "was abandoned at the end of the 4th millennium BC"; "Post-Uruk and Nineveh 5 in northern Mesopotamia" follow, which no dossier draws.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: the core is the alluvium, the outposts are radii around excavated colonies; nothing is a frontier.

notes: Culture dossier; the Uruk period proper ends c. 3300/3100 BC but Cliopatria draws the Sumerian City-States from 3400 BCE and Elam from 3200 BCE, so the core is handed over in 3400 and Susiana in 3200 BCE, and the dossier ends in 3200 BCE with the desertion of the colonies. The Jemdet Nasr phase (c. 3200/3100-3000 BC) falls inside the Sumerian row. Disagreement: Uruk start 4000 BC (this page) vs Ubaid end 3800 BC (Ubaid page). Gazetteer: Habuba Kabira, Jebel Aruda, Tell Brak, Godin Tepe, Hacinebi and Arslantepe are not places; a coordinate radius (Habuba Kabira) and radii around Kermanshah, Al Hasakah, Malatya and the Sanliurfa province stand in. The me-01 sumerian-city-states dossier lists no predecessor; it should name uruk-period.
